title: Poset-nerve tests detect cardinal filteredness of quasicategories
statement: Use the universes, infinite regular cardinals, $\kappa$-small simplicial sets and $\kappa$-filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and quasicategories, ordinary nerves and coherent cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory in the containing universe. For a small partially ordered set $B$, let $B^{\triangleright}=B\amalg\{\infty\}$, with its original order and $b<\infty$ for every $b\in B$. The following are equivalent: $\mathcal E$ is $\kappa$-filtered; for every partially ordered set $B$ with $|B|<\kappa$ and every simplicial map $p:N(B)\to\mathcal E$, there exists a simplicial map $\bar p:N(B^{\triangleright})\to\mathcal E$ whose restriction to $N(B)$ is $p$. The empty poset is included, so the second condition requires that $\mathcal E$ be nonempty. No existence of colimits in $\mathcal E$ is assumed.

source.place: Remark 5.3.1.12, printed p.383 (PDF p.400), including the finite-cardinal case via Variant 4.2.3.16 and the uncountable case via Variant 4.2.3.15. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical criterion.

proof.text: Let $B$ be a partially ordered set with $|B|<\kappa$ and $p:N(B)\to\mathcal E$. The nerve $N(B)$ is $\kappa$-small: its nondegenerate $n$-simplices are the strictly increasing chains $b_0<\cdots<b_n$ in $B$, so there are finitely many when $B$ is finite, and when $B$ is infinite their set has cardinality $|B|<\kappa$. Since $\mathcal E$ is $\kappa$-filtered, [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] gives a coherent cocone $p\to\Delta_{N(B)}T$, that is, a vertex of the coherent cocone category $P_p$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. By [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] the comparison $J_p\to P_p$ from the join slice is a functor equivalence; a quasi-inverse carries this vertex to a vertex of $J_p$, that is, a map $N(B)\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $p$. Finally $N(B)\star\Delta^0=N(B^{\triangleright})$: an $n$-simplex of $N(B^{\triangleright})$ is a weakly increasing chain $c_0\leq\cdots\leq c_n$ in $B^{\triangleright}$, and since $\infty$ is the maximum, the entries in $B$ form an initial block $c_0,\ldots,c_a$ ($-1\leq a\leq n$) followed by the constant block at $\infty$; this is exactly the decomposition of an $n$-simplex of the join into an $N(B)$-block and a $\Delta^0$-block, and restriction of chains is the join's operator. So $p$ extends over $N(B^{\triangleright})$.

source.place: Remark 5.3.1.12, 'only if' direction ("obvious"), with Definition 5.3.1.7 (join-cone filteredness), compared with coherent cocones through Proposition 4.2.1.5

proof.text: Conversely, assume that every map $N(B)\to\mathcal E$ with $|B|<\kappa$ extends over $N(B^{\triangleright})$. Let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and $p:K\to\mathcal E$ a coherent diagram. By [lem-coef-infinity-poset-nerve-cofinal-replacement] there are a partially ordered set $B$ with $|B|<\kappa$ and a map $\varphi:N(B)\to K$ such that, for every vertex $T$ of $\mathcal E$, restriction $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_KT)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(B),\mathcal E)}(p\varphi,\Delta_{N(B)}T)$ is an equivalence of Kan complexes. Put $q=p\varphi$. By hypothesis $q$ extends to $\bar q:N(B^{\triangleright})=N(B)\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal E$ (identification of step 1), a vertex of the join slice $J_q$ with apex $T=\bar q(\infty)$. The comparison $J_q\to P_q$ of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] lies over $\mathcal E$, so it carries $\bar q$ to a vertex of $P_q$ over $T$: an edge $q\to\Delta_{N(B)}T$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(B),\mathcal E)$, i.e. a vertex of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(B),\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_{N(B)}T)$ (vertices of the right-pinched mapping space of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] are exactly such edges). An equivalence of Kan complexes is a bijection on path components, so $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_KT)$ has a vertex, which is a coherent cocone $p\to\Delta_KT$. Thus every $\kappa$-small diagram in $\mathcal E$ has a cocone, and $\mathcal E$ is $\kappa$-filtered by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. For $K=\varnothing$ the poset $B$ is empty (a map $N(B)\to\varnothing$ forces $B=\varnothing$) and the assumed extension of the empty map is a vertex of $\mathcal E$, which is the required cocone; no colimits in $\mathcal E$ are used.
